Goal: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.
Parent hypotheses (starting points): Parent 1:
TITLE: Empirical p-value fusion across levels and branches (Fisher-MVFA)
SUMMARY: Turn each level/branch patch score into an empirical p-value against support-normal LOO scores and combine them with Fisher's method, giving a per-image, distribution-free anomaly statistic and a principled threshold.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD modalities, Fisher p-value fusion matches MVFA's transductive fusion within 1 AUROC point for K >= 4, and its support-derived threshold achieves a realised false-positive rate within 5 points of nominal, whereas a raw-sum per-image fusion without test-set normalisation loses at least 3 AUROC points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: combination rule (raw sum + test-set min-max vs. empirical p-value fusion). For each branch b and level l, the null distribution is the set of LOO patch scores of the K support normals. A test patch score s gets p_bl = (1 + #{null >= s}) / (1 + N_null). The fused pixel statistic is X = -2 * sum_{b,l} log p_bl (Fisher), and the image statistic is the mean of the top 2% pixels of X. Because X is built from tail probabilities, a threshold can be read from the support LOO image statistics. Dependent variables: AUROC (image, pixel), PRO, thresholded sensitivity/specificity/F1, ECE, and per-level contribution analysis.
RATIONALE: MVFA and MLCA add the four levels' raw maps and then min-max them over the test set; levels have different score scales, so the sum is dominated by whichever level has the largest spread. Converting every level and branch score into an empirical tail probability against the support normals puts all evidence on a common, calibrated scale and makes the combination inductive.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: add null_scores(supports) returning, per branch and level, the sorted 1-D array of LOO patch scores (K x 289 values) and empirical_p(s, null) via np.searchsorted. 2) test_few.py: for each test image compute p_bl for all 289 patches at each of 4 levels and 2 branches, X_patch = -2 sum log p (16 x 16-bit floats per patch), bilinearly upsample X to 240x240; image score = mean of top 2%. 3) Ties and extreme scores: p is floored at 1/(1+N_null), so X is bounded. 4) Threshold: 95th percentile of the support LOO image statistics. 5) Variant: weighted Fisher with level weights estimated from the separability of LOO normals vs. the other branch (no target labels). 6) No retraining.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: transductive MVFA fusion; per-image raw sum; LOO-Z (z-score fusion) as a parametric alternative. Ablations: Fisher vs. Stouffer vs. min-p combination; per-level vs. all-level null pools; aggregation operator. Metrics as in the problem. Falsification: AUROC loss above 2 points or realised FPR deviating by more than 10 points from nominal.

Parent 2:
TITLE: Bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion (LOO-Z) for per-image MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Standardise MVFA's zero-shot and few-shot maps with leave-one-out statistics of the K support normals, clip them to a bounded range, fuse with inverse-variance weights and pool the top 2% pixels, so every image is scored on its own.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, LOO-Z fusion achieves image- and pixel-level AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's transductive fusion while its AUROC varies at least 3x less across random 50% test subsamples and 10%/50% prevalence resamples, and its support-derived threshold yields realised specificity within 5 points of the nominal 95%.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: the fusion rule (transductive test-set min-max + 0.5 sum vs. LOO-Z). LOO-Z computes, for each branch b in {zero, few} and level l, the mean and standard deviation of patch scores of the K support normals, where the few-shot score of support i is computed against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports (leave-one-out) and the zero-shot score uses the text anchors as usual. Each test patch score is converted to z = (s - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, clipped to [-3, 6] (bounded drift), summed over levels, and the two branches are combined with weights w_b proportional to 1/Var(LOO image scores of branch b). The image score is the mean of the top 2% fused pixels. Dependent variables: image-/pixel-level AUROC, sensitivity/specificity/F1 at the threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores, ECE of the logistic-mapped score, and the stability of AUROC under test-set subsampling and prevalence shift.
RATIONALE: The chain moves from MVFA's transductive fusion (test-set min-max, fixed 0.5) to methods that score each image against references only (MadCLIP) and that bound how far a per-image adjustment can move (ReCAP). The missing step for MVFA is to replace test-set statistics with reference statistics from the K normal supports and to bound each branch's contribution so neither dominates, which yields a deployable per-image score and a threshold that can be set before seeing target labels.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: refactor scoring into score_image(x, supports) that never touches other test images. 2) Support statistics (new function support_stats in utils.py): for each support normal i, build memory banks from the other K-1 supports at each level l (det and seg tokens as in MVFA), compute few-shot patch scores 1 - max cos; compute zero-shot patch scores softmax(100 * f_l @ T)[abnormal]; store mu_bl, sigma_bl (sigma floored at 1e-3) and the LOO image scores. For K=2 the LOO bank contains a single image; statistics are pooled over all 289 patches x 4 levels so they remain defined. 3) For a test image: z_bl = clip((s_bl - mu_bl)/sigma_bl, -3, 6); Z_b = sum_l z_bl upsampled to 240x240; F = w_zero Z_zero + w_few Z_few with w_b = (1/v_b)/(1/v_zero + 1/v_few), v_b the variance of branch b's LOO image scores. 4) Image score = mean of top 2% of F (about 1,150 of 57,600 pixels; ablations: max, mean, top 1%, top 5%). 5) Threshold tau = 95th percentile of support LOO image scores; probability via Platt mapping fitted on support LOO scores with pseudo-negatives only is not identifiable, so ECE is computed after mapping p = sigmoid((score - tau)/s) with s = support score IQR. 6) No training changes; reuse MVFA checkpoints trained under the shared protocol.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: MVFA transductive fusion (released code); MVFA with per-image fusion but no normalisation (raw sum); LOO-Z without clipping; LOO-Z with equal weights. Ablations: aggregation operator; K. Metrics: image AUROC, pixel AUROC, PRO; sensitivity, specificity, F1 at tau; ECE; AUROC standard deviation over 20 random 50% test subsamples and under prevalence resampling to 10% and 50% abnormal. Falsification: if LOO-Z loses more than 2 AUROC points on average, or its AUROC is not more stable than the transductive fusion, the hypothesis is rejected.
